subject: Latent regression models for multiple groups

messages.author: 885539f3f5ae8fd5
messages.subject: Latent regression models for multiple groups
parts:
Hey Phil!

Long-time user here. I just tried fitting a multipleGroup model while specifying covdata and formula as additional arguments and saw that latent regression models aren't supported for multiple groups yet. The 'yet' in that error message gave me hope. :) Just wondering if this is something you think will be supported in the near future, or is this really far down the list? Thanks!

- Jon

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Latent regression models for multiple groups
parts:
Hi Jon,

It's certainly on the TODO list, but it is admittedly a little lower for structural reasons. I first would like to allow for the better Oakes SE method to support latent regression models, and then once this is in place adding multi-group latent regression models would be more useful (Wald tests and SEs would be readily available). I'm not sure of any timeline (I'm just getting settled after making another large international move for work), but perhaps check the activity on Github once in a while to see if I've made any progress? Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Latent regression models for multiple groups
parts:
The formula input to mirt() allows for a list of formulas, where the left hand side of the ~ can be the explicit dimension. So if you named two factors F1 and F2 you could provide an input such as 

mirt(..., formula = list(F1 ~ cov1 + cov2, F2 ~ cov3))

HTH.

Phil
